title: World geography
description: The continents, oceans, great rivers and capitals you need to picture the world map.

ideas.title: Continents and oceans
ideas.summary: The land is conventionally divided into seven continents and the sea into five oceans.

items.q: Which continent is the largest in both area and population?
Which is the largest and deepest of the world's oceans?
In the seven-continent model, which continent is smallest by land area?
Which continent has the most UN member states?
Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?

ideas.title: Lines on the globe
ideas.summary: Latitude measures north and south of the equator; longitude measures east and west of the prime meridian.

items.q: What do lines of latitude measure on a globe?
items.a: Distance north or south of the equator, in degrees

items.q: Through which district of London does the prime meridian, 0 degrees longitude, pass?
At about what latitude do the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn lie?
items.a: About 23.5 degrees north and 23.5 degrees south

items.q: Which line of longitude does the International Date Line roughly follow?

ideas.title: Mountains, rivers and deserts
ideas.summary: A few great features anchor the physical map: the Himalayas and Andes, the Nile and Amazon, the Sahara.

items.q: What is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level, and in which range does it stand?
Which river carries more water than any other on Earth?
Which river, flowing north through Egypt to the Mediterranean, is the longest in Africa?
What is the longest mountain range on land, running down the western edge of South America?
What is the largest hot desert in the world?

ideas.title: Countries and capitals
ideas.summary: Some capitals and superlatives are worth knowing cold, especially the ones people often get wrong.

items.q: Which country is the largest in the world by area?
Which two countries are by far the most populous in the world?
What is the capital of Australia?
What is the capital of Canada?
What is the capital of Brazil?
What is the capital of Turkey?

ideas.title: Straits and canals
ideas.summary: Narrow passages, natural and dug, join the seas and carry much of the world's shipping.

items.q: Which canal, opened in 1869, links the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea?
Which canal, opened in 1914, links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans across Central America?
Which strait separates Spain from Morocco and joins the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea?
Which strait separates Russia from Alaska, and so Asia from North America?
